Imagine… you get struck by lightning.
What would happen to your body?
You are standing in an open field.
The air smells like metal.
Your hair… starts to rise.
Then.
Three hundred million volts.
In a split second, the air around you heats to thirty thousand degrees.
Five times hotter than the surface of the Sun.
The rain on your skin turns to steam.
Your shoes can be blown right off.
And your heart… stops.
But often, most of the current flashes over your skin, not through you.
It leaves a strange mark.
A red, fern-like pattern, called a Lichtenberg figure.
With fast help, nine out of ten people survive.
One park ranger was struck seven times… and lived.
So remember.
If you can hear thunder… you are close enough to be struck.
